title: De quibusdam eximiis proprietatibus circa divisores potestatum occurrentibus

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages): P = 4n+1 is prime, and 'residua' are the quadratic residues mod P. Writing P = 4p + (2q+1)^2, i.e. p = n - q(q+1), Euler has shown (§9) that every number n - qq - q, and also its negative qq + q - n, is a residue, since -1 is a residue for P ≡ 1 (mod 4).

End of §11: residues are closed under products and powers. Hence if αγ and βγ are residues, so is αβ, because αβγ² is a residue and the square γ² can be dropped.

§12 (Cor. 3): if αβ and α are residues, then β is a residue.

§13 (Scholion): since such combinations can be made in infinitely many ways, Euler finds it 'maxime verisimile' that every prime factor of the numbers |n - q(q+1)| is itself a residue mod P. He tests this inductively.
- He lists q(q+1) = 0, 2, 6, 12, ..., 420.
- For each prime P he factors the values p = |n - q(q+1)|, q = 0, 1, 2, ..., and collects the prime factors r.
- This page covers the cases P = 5, 13, 17, 29, 37, 41, 53, 61; the next pages run up to 197.
- §14 states that the property is found by induction alone and has no firm proof.

In modern terms, (2q+1)² - 4(q²+q-n) = P. So for any odd prime ℓ dividing q²+q-n, P ≡ (2q+1)² (mod ℓ), i.e. (P/ℓ) = 1. Euler's conjecture that then (ℓ/P) = 1 is exactly quadratic reciprocity for P ≡ 1 (mod 4).
- Since every odd prime ℓ arises in this way for a suitable q, the conjecture is equivalent to that case of the law, which Gauss proved in 1796/1801.
- For ℓ = 2: q²+q-n is even only if n is even, i.e. P ≡ 1 (mod 8), and then 2 is a residue. This is consistent with the second supplementary law.
errors: Case 2° (P=13, n=3): the value for q=4, 20-3=17, is omitted. The printed list 3,1,3,3²,3³,3·13,53,3·23 skips from 9 straight to 27. Consequently the prime 17, which is a residue (17≡4 mod 13), is missing from the r-list.

Case 5° (P=37, n=9): several printed values are wrong. The correct values for q=0..10 are 9, 7, 3, 3, 11, 21=3·7, 33=3·11, 47, 63=3²·7, 81=3⁴, 101. Euler prints 19, 43, 59 and 7·11 in place of 21, 47, 63 and 81. The r-list therefore wrongly contains 19, 43 and 59, which are quadratic NON-residues mod 37 (19, 6 and 22 mod 37). The printed table thus seemingly contradicts the very conjecture it is meant to support. The correct r-list is 1, 3, 7, 11, 47, 101 (47≡10 and 101≡27 are both residues).
The other cases on this page (P=5, 17, 29, 41, 53, 61) check out correctly.

ideas.what: Quadratic residues are closed under multiplication; if αγ and βγ (or αβ and α) are residues, then αβ (resp. β) is a residue
ideas.modern_name: Multiplicativity of the Legendre symbol / the residues form an index-2 subgroup of (Z/P)*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Theoremata circa residua, E262 and related papers); Legendre for the symbol
ideas.where_published: E262 and other residue papers (Opera omnia I.2-I.4)

ideas.what: Conjecture, supported by tables, that every prime factor of |n - q(q+1)| is a quadratic residue mod the prime 4n+1
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic reciprocity for P ≡ 1 (mod 4), in the form: ℓ | x² - P implies (ℓ/P) = 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (conjectural forms, e.g. E164, E552), Legendre (1785), Gauss (first proof, 1801)
ideas.where_published: E164 'Theoremata circa divisores numerorum in hac forma pa^2±qb^2 contentorum' and E552; this paper E557 (Opuscula analytica I, 1783; Opera omnia I.3)

missed.claim: The printed numerical evidence for P=37 contains arithmetic errors that produce apparent counterexamples to Euler's own conjecture: 19, 43 and 59 are non-residues mod 37. There is also an omission (17) in the P=13 case. I am unsure whether the Opera omnia edition flags these.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor philological point for editors and historians reading Euler's inductive evidence for reciprocity. It does not affect the mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a known Euler induction toward quadratic reciprocity, already documented in histories of the reciprocity law. The only novelty is a few unflagged table errors, which happen to produce apparent counterexamples.
transcription_corrections: No substantive transcription errors relative to the image on this page. The faulty entries in 2° (missing 17) and 5° (19, 43, 59, 7·11) are faithful to the printed original, not transcription mistakes.
